newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: United States backs U.N. mediation in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: United States backs U.N. mediation in Afghanistan.

text.p: The United States wants the United Nations to mediate in the Afghanistan conflict, believing that no one country can handle the task, a U.S. official said on Tuesday.

"We believe that the U.N. is in the best position to mediate among the relevant parties in Kabul," the Assistant Secretary of State for South Asian Affairs, Robin Raphel, told a news conference in Dhaka.

"We are very much behind the creation of a special U.N. mission...we do not think any single country can do it," said Raphel, in Bangladesh on the last leg of a South Asia tour. She has already visited Pakistan and India.
She dismissed speculation that Washington was backing the Taleban administration, which captured the Afghan capital Kabul last September and now controls most of the country.
"We do not recognise the Talebans. We do not support any of the parties there. We only want a government in Kabul which is acceptable to all the people of Afghanistan."
Raphel said Washington was seriously concerned over the conflict in Afghanistan which, she said, threatened regional stability.
"The trouble is pushing refugees across the border which is our primary concern."
Raphel said the United States was worried over the effect of a prolonged Afghan conflict on the narcotics trade and international terrorism.
Raphel said the U.S. administration in President Bill Clinton's second term considered South Asia a "very important region".
"All the economies here (in South Asia) are opening up. They are gradually joining the free market system. Also this is a very important strategic location," she said.
Raphel was due to leave for home later on Tuesday at the end of a five-day stay in Dhaka where she chaired a meeting of U.S. ambassadors in South Asia.
